Brand exploration · Round 1 · October 2026

Brainfence protects your head from a loud, fast world. Every asset on this page comes out of one generator, so a new palette or concept shows up everywhere at once.

Icon concepts

Each concept comes in three variants. The poster adds halftone and scanlines, the icon is a flat tile for app stores and docks, and mono is a single-color template for Android themed icons, the macOS menu bar and the Windows tray.

App palette

Foil was picked, and all three apps now use it from shared/tokens.json. They used to use Material’s stock purple, which isn’t in the icon anywhere. These are the three ways to carry the Static palette into the apps, each with a light and a dark theme. Every color comes from a brand color’s tonal ramp, and the dark themes use the icon’s exact void and neon.

Light mode is the hard part. Lime and cyan are light colors, so on white they can only be fills, never text. The ramps below show what each brand color becomes at every tone. Each direction also adds three colors for blocking state, so every client shows blocked, unlocked and pending the same way.

Foil

Closest to the icon. Surfaces and buttons are foil greys, black on light and white on dark, and neon only shows up where it means something: lime for the main action and anything unlocked, magenta when something is blocked, cyan for timers and time locks.

Hazard

Lime leads. Every primary action is the icon’s lime, and lime is a light color, so light mode can’t use it for text or button fills. There it darkens to an acid olive, and the bright lime only appears as container fills. Magenta still means blocked, cyan means unlocked, and amber marks a pending change.

Signal

Magenta leads, the brain inside the crown. It holds up best in light mode, where a deep raspberry has plenty of contrast. Blocking is the app’s job, so a block screen is magenta too, not an error. Errors shift to orange-red so they stay distinct, lime means unlocked and cyan means pending.

Fence Stencil

The house type is a full A–Z on a 4×6 grid, with chamfered corners and a 12° forward slant. Taglines, headers and merch can all be set in it straight from code.

Source

npm run brand                  rebuild everything into branding/out/
branding/src/palettes.mjs      add a palette: every asset gains a version in it
branding/src/rounds.mjs        which concepts and palettes each round shows
branding/src/marks/*.mjs       round 1 concepts (kept as reviewed)
branding/src/marks/crowns/     round 2: guy.mjs plus one file per fence crown
branding/src/type.mjs          Fence Stencil glyphs and text setting
branding/src/fx.mjs            RGB split, glitch slices, streaks, halftone, fence lattice
branding/src/compose.mjs       icon, poster and mono variants, lockups, banner
branding/src/schemes.mjs       round 4: app palette directions and contrast checks
branding/src/color.mjs         tonal ramps (L* tones) and WCAG contrast
branding/src/app-palette.mjs   round 4 mock screens, role lists, contrast tables
branding/out/marks/<id>/       <id>-<palette>-icon.svg, -poster.svg, <id>-mono.svg
